issues.t: Front wheel hub can shift out of the steering knuckle
issues.sym: ABS, traction control or anti-skid warnings come on, sometimes with a blind-spot (BLIS) 'reduced function' message. You may hear grinding or feel looseness at a front wheel.
issues.why: On these cars the front wheel bearing can slowly work its way out of its seat in the steering knuckle. That moves the wheel-speed sensor out of position and, if ignored, can let the hub come loose. Volvo issued bulletins adding a retainer bracket and, in worse cases, replacing the hub or knuckle.
issues.next: Treat a grinding front wheel or new ABS/BLIS warnings as urgent and have the front hubs inspected soon. Ask the shop about the Volvo bearing retainer bulletin.

issues.t: Clogged PCV oil trap causes whistling and oil leaks
issues.sym: A whistle or squeal from the engine that stops when you take off the oil filler cap, oil leaks around the engine seals, a rough idle or a check engine light.
issues.why: The crankcase breather (oil trap) and its hoses clog with sludge or the diaphragm tears. Pressure builds inside the engine and pushes oil past seals, and can harm the turbo if left alone.
issues.next: Have the breather system checked soon. Fixing it early is far cheaper than replacing leaking seals or a turbo later. Regular synthetic oil changes help prevent it.

issues.t: Timing belt or idler pulley failure can wreck the engine
issues.sym: Often no warning before failure. A chirp, squeal or rattle from the belt area can come first. If the belt breaks or jumps, the engine stops and won't restart.
issues.why: The T5 uses a rubber timing belt with tensioner and idler pulleys. A worn belt or a failed pulley can let the belt slip, and in this engine the valves can then hit the pistons. One C30 owner lost an engine when an idler pulley failed.
issues.next: If your car is near 10 years old or past about 100,000 miles with no record of a belt change, have the timing belt, pulleys and water pump replaced. Don't wait for noises.

issues.t: Front camshaft seal oil leak
issues.sym: Oil drips at the front (timing belt end) of the engine, a burning-oil smell, or oil on the timing belt cover.
issues.why: The camshaft seals harden with age, and crankcase pressure from a clogged PCV system can push them out.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. Oil on the timing belt shortens its life, so this is often done along with the belt and a PCV check.

issues.t: Coolant expansion tank cracks and leaks
issues.sym: Coolant smell, low coolant warning, or pink/green fluid sprayed around the engine bay.
issues.why: The plastic coolant expansion tank cracks with age and heat cycles. Several C30 owners report tanks that cracked or burst.
issues.next: Check the tank for cracks when the engine is cold. Top up with the correct coolant and replace the tank soon so the engine doesn't overheat.

issues.t: Turbo boost control valve failure
issues.sym: Low power, especially above mid revs, a check engine light, or a whistling or hissing sound from the engine.
issues.why: The solenoid valve that controls turbo boost, or the turbo breather valve, sticks or wears out, so the turbo can't build pressure properly.
issues.next: Have the boost control system and vacuum hoses checked with a scan tool. It's usually a small part, but don't ignore a turbo that won't boost.

issues.t: Fuel pressure sensor failure
issues.sym: Hard starting, stalling, hesitation or a check engine light with fuel pressure codes.
issues.why: The fuel rail pressure sensor gives wrong readings as it ages, so the engine computer delivers the wrong amount of fuel.
issues.next: A shop can confirm it by reading live fuel pressure data. Replacing the sensor is usually quick.

issues.t: Reduced engine power warning from accelerator pedal or throttle faults
issues.sym: A 'reduced engine power' message, the car won't accelerate normally, sometimes only in cold weather.
issues.why: Faults in the accelerator pedal sensor, its wiring or connector, or the electronic throttle body make the engine computer limit power to protect you.
issues.next: Drive gently to a safe place and have the codes read. Wiring and connector problems are common, so ask the shop to check them before replacing parts.

issues.t: Misfire from a failed ignition coil
issues.sym: Flashing or steady check engine light, rough idle, shaking and loss of power.
issues.why: One of the five ignition coils or a worn spark plug stops firing properly.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.

issues.t: Electric radiator fan fails
issues.sym: Temperature gauge climbs in traffic, A/C stops cooling at idle, or the fan runs nonstop or not at all.
issues.why: The electric cooling fan motor or its control module burns out. Without the fan the engine can overheat when the car isn't moving.
issues.next: If the temperature warning comes on, pull over safely and shut the engine off. Have the fan tested before driving in traffic or hot weather.

issues.t: Check engine light from failed EVAP leak detection pump
issues.sym: Check engine light with evaporative system codes. The car drives normally.
issues.why: The pump that tests the fuel vapor system for leaks wears out.
issues.next: Make sure the gas cap is tight first. If the light stays on, have the EVAP system tested; this is not urgent but will fail an emissions test.

issues.t: Worn engine mounts cause vibration
issues.sym: Vibration through the cabin at idle or when accelerating, and clunks when shifting or taking off.
issues.why: The fluid-filled and rubber engine mounts deflate or crack with age.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected. Worn mounts add stress to axles and exhaust parts.

issues.t: Harsh or jerky automatic shifts
issues.sym: A thump or jerk when the automatic downshifts from 5th to 4th, slipping, or delayed engagement into gear.
issues.why: Volvo issued a bulletin for rough 5th-to-4th shifts on these cars. Some cars with higher miles have needed a valve body, torque converter or a replacement transmission.
issues.next: Ask a Volvo specialist to check fluid level and condition, look for software updates, and reset the shift adaptation before agreeing to major repairs.

issues.t: Clutch or dual-mass flywheel wear on manual cars
issues.sym: Clutch slips, engine revs rise without speed, chatter on takeoff, or a rattle at idle that stops when the clutch pedal is pressed.
issues.why: The clutch wears normally with use. The dual-mass flywheel behind it can also wear out and is often replaced at the same time.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm whether the flywheel needs replacing along with the clutch. Avoid hard launches until it's fixed.

issues.t: Torn CV boots and worn front axles
issues.sym: Clicking when turning, grease on the inside of the front wheels, or vibration when accelerating.
issues.why: The rubber boots on the front axles crack and let grease out and dirt in, which wears the CV joints. Owners report this as one of the most common C30 repairs.
issues.next: Ask for a look at the boots at every oil change. Replacing a boot early is cheaper than a whole axle.

issues.t: Noisy wheel bearings
issues.sym: A hum or growl that gets louder with speed and may change when you steer left or right.
issues.why: Wheel bearings wear out. TrueDelta owners list bearings and hubs among the most common C30 repairs.
issues.next: Have the noisy corner identified. A badly worn bearing can affect braking and ABS.

issues.t: Worn struts and strut mounts
issues.sym: Clunks or creaks over bumps, a bouncy ride, or a creak when turning the steering wheel.
issues.why: The front struts and their top mounts and bearings wear out. Struts and strut bearings are among the most reported C30 suspension repairs.
issues.next: Have the suspension inspected. Struts are usually replaced in pairs and need an alignment afterward.

issues.t: Worn sway bar links and bushings
issues.sym: Rattling or knocking over small bumps, mostly at low speed.
issues.why: The links and rubber bushings for the sway bar wear out over time.
issues.next: Not urgent, but have it checked so you know the noise isn't something more serious.

issues.t: Worn control arm bushings
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, loose or wandering steering, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The rubber bushings in the front and rear control arms wear and crack.
issues.next: Have the suspension checked and get an alignment afterward to protect your tires.

issues.t: Broken front coil springs
issues.sym: A loud clunk or bang over bumps, the car sitting lower at one corner, or a tire rubbing.
issues.why: Front coil springs can rust and snap, often at the bottom coil.
issues.next: Have it checked soon. A broken spring can cut into a tire. Springs are replaced in pairs.

issues.t: Sunroof drains clog and leak water inside
issues.sym: Wet headliner, damp carpets (front or rear), or water dripping after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: The drain tubes at the sunroof corners clog or come loose, so water overflows into the cabin.
issues.next: Clear the drains soon and dry the carpets fully to prevent mold and electrical damage.

issues.t: Windshield seal leaks water into the cabin
issues.sym: Water in the driver's footwell after rain, sometimes spreading to the rear floor, or a stained headliner.
issues.why: Some windshields were not sealed well at the factory, so the glass can move slightly and let water in.
issues.next: Have a glass shop test the seal. Dry the carpets quickly to stop mold and protect wiring under the floor.

issues.t: A/C compressor or clutch failure
issues.sym: Air conditioning blows warm, cycles on and off, or the compressor makes noise.
issues.why: The A/C compressor or its clutch wears out. Owners also report leaking valves and condensers.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested first. A recharge alone won't last if there is a leak.

issues.t: Alternator failure
issues.sym: Battery warning light, dim lights, or a dead battery soon after a new one.
issues.why: The alternator wears out with age, and oil leaks onto it can speed that up.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested before buying another battery.

issues.t: Battery drains overnight from the satellite radio receiver
issues.sym: Dead or weak battery after the car sits, sometimes with radio or satellite radio faults. A new battery may die again.
issues.why: The satellite radio receiver (RDAR) can stay awake after the car is off and slowly drain the battery. Volvo issued a bulletin to replace it.
issues.next: Ask a Volvo dealer or specialist to check for parasitic drain and the RDAR bulletin before replacing the battery again.

issues.t: Steering lock fault stops the car from starting
issues.sym: The car won't start and shows 'Turn steering try start again', or there is no click from the column when you insert the key.
issues.why: The electric steering column lock sticks in place. Volvo dropped this lock from the 2009 and later C30.
issues.next: Turn the wheel gently while removing and reinserting the key. If it keeps happening, the lock needs repair or replacement and programming by a dealer.

issues.t: Airbag light from passenger seat sensor or wiring
issues.sym: Airbag (SRS) warning light, or the passenger airbag 'off' light acting wrong with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: The passenger seat weight sensor fails, or wiring under the seat comes loose or shorts.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read soon. The airbag may not work as designed while the light is on.

issues.t: Xenon headlight bulb or ballast failure
issues.sym: One headlight goes out or flickers, often with a bulb warning.
issues.why: HID (xenon) bulbs and their control modules wear out. Headlight bulbs are among the common C30 complaints.
issues.next: Replace bulbs in pairs so the color matches. If a new bulb doesn't fix it, the ballast or module is likely bad.

issues.t: Rear brake caliper or parking brake sticks
issues.sym: A dragging or grinding noise from the rear, a hot rear wheel, the car pulling, or a parking brake that won't release.
issues.why: Rear caliper pistons and parking brake cables corrode and stick, especially in salty climates.
issues.next: Have the rear brakes inspected. A dragging brake wears pads fast and can overheat.

issues.t: Power steering hose can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaks and the steering suddenly becomes very heavy.
issues.why: A defective power steering hose could leak fluid quickly and cause a complete loss of power assist.
issues.next: Check with a Volvo dealer whether recall 08V329 was done on your car.

issues.t: Manual gearshift lever stud can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: The gear lever feels loose or won't select gears properly.
issues.why: A problem with the gearshift lever stud assembly could make shifting unreliable and raise crash risk.
issues.next: Check with a Volvo dealer whether recall 10V255 was done on your car.

issues.t: Dealer portable GPS battery can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: The portable Garmin navigation unit gets hot or swells.
issues.why: The battery in some dealer-supplied portable Garmin GPS units could overheat and start a fire.
issues.next: Unplug the unit and keep it out of the car until you confirm recall 10V566 was done.
